edges.description: Lysosomal TPP1 deficiency drives progressive motor and language decline, cognitive impairment, seizures, and early death.
TPP1 deficiency also drives retinal degeneration that can continue despite CNS-directed therapy.
Cortical neuronal lysosomal storage and neurodegeneration manifest clinically with childhood-onset seizures.
Progressive neuronal loss across cerebral and cerebellar networks drives loss of previously acquired language and cognitive milestones.
Cerebellar neuronal degeneration produces early and near-universal gait and limb ataxia.
Cortical and subcortical hyperexcitability from neuronal storage pathology causes prominent myoclonus.
Progressive corticospinal tract degeneration leads to spasticity during the middle stage of CLN2 movement-disorder evolution.
Basal ganglia and extrapyramidal circuit involvement produces dystonia in over half of patients.
Advanced neurodegeneration progresses from early ataxia/myoclonus and mid-stage spasticity/dystonia to late-stage hypokinesia.
Cumulative cerebellar, pyramidal, and extrapyramidal neurodegeneration causes relentless deterioration of motor function.
Progressive degeneration of retinal photoreceptors leads to central visual loss and eventual blindness.
Lysosomal storage accumulation in photoreceptor cells drives bilateral progressive retinal dystrophy.
